argument: Evaluate y-3x+1 at the three ordered pairs: values are 0,1,-4 respectively, so only the first belongs.
All points (2,t) satisfy x=2 and share one horizontal position; y=2 is horizontal and y=x² contains noncollinear points.
The zero sets coincide because the original residual equals twice x+y-4. At (4,0), the second fails; at (0,4), the third fails.
At (3,-2) both squared displacement terms vanish; translating x by 3 and y by -2 converts the equation to a radius-2 circle at the origin.
Multiplication by -3 is bijective on reals. Variable multiplication admits zeros, while squaring identifies opposite signs, so neither alternative guarantees equal zero sets.
The first point makes xy-x²=0 and y-x=2. The second satisfies both equations, and the third fails the multiplied equation.
The real numbers have no zero divisors; the factored equation holds iff y=x or y=-x. Point (1,-1) refutes the second candidate; (1,1) refutes the third.
The equation reduces independently of coordinates to false statement 0=1. This is why the line definition excludes both linear coefficients zero.
Nonnegative summands with zero sum are each zero, implying x=y=0. Substitution confirms existence, excluding the empty-set option.
Set difference ({x=0} union {y=1}) minus {y=1} equals {x=0,y≠1}. The alternatives already lie on the retained horizontal line.
For any solution of y²=x, x is nonnegative. Restricting y to nonnegative chooses the unique principal root; y≤0 chooses the other branch, and x>0 retains two branches.
